title: interleaved-capture-tiling-and-kernel-hash-fallback-to-reduce-warmup-thrashing
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring warmup regressions in mixed-workload tenants where continuous batching interleaves short and long sequences. Captures taken across interleaved KV cache offsets produced graphs that were fragile to small kernel-selection differences; replays would either miss hot paths or trigger repeated fallback recompilations, causing 30–70% p50 latency degradation during warmup windows. This PR introduces a split-capture (tiling) strategy combined with a kernel-hash compatibility fallback to minimize thrashing and dramatically shorten warmup.

Design summary: single-string design doc below.

- Split-capture tiling: instead of capturing one large graph covering a wide sequence-length distribution, the capture manager partitions incoming requests into "tiles" by sequence-length and KV-offset proximity and performs targeted captures per tile. Tiles are small, deterministic buckets (configurable: default 16 tokens width) so captured kernels are stable and more likely to match replayed kernels.
- Kernel-hash compatibility fallback: when replay encounters a kernel mismatch, we compute a lightweight kernel-hash fingerprint for the active kernels in the current graph and consult a compatibility policy that either accepts the mismatch (if hash distance under threshold), triggers a fast-local patch (stitching minor kernel variants), or falls back to recompiled capture. This reduces full fallbacks when only minor codegen differences exist.
- KV-alignment metadata: captures now embed KV-offset markers into the graph metadata so replay aligns the cached KV entries deterministically. This avoids misaligned KV-cache offsets that were a major source of mismatch for interleaved workloads.
- Scheduler hints: new scheduler flag for continuous batching signals the capture manager to avoid mixing tiles from >1 priority lane into the same capture epoch. This preserves capture homogeneity for mixed-priority traffic.
- Deterministic incremental warmup: when a new tile is first observed, we perform a short deterministic warmup (default 4 priming requests) with guaranteed kernel-selection seeding to avoid long probabilistic priming.

Checklist (this PR):
- [x] Implement split-capture tiling in runtime/cuda/capture_manager (tiling policy + config)
- [x] Add kernel-hash library and compatibility policy logic (runtime/cuda/kernel_hash.h/.cc)
- [x] Embed KV-alignment metadata during capture and interpret during replay (runtime/kv_cache/kv_align.*)
- [x] Add scheduler hint plumbing and default continuous-batching policies (runtime/scheduler/)
- [x] Add deterministic incremental warmup path with configurable priming length
- [x] Unit + E2E tests for replay resiliency and KV alignment (tests/e2e/cudagraph_warmup_test.py)
- [x] Benchmarks and CI perf jobs updated (benchmarks/ci/graph_replay_latency.yaml)
- [x] Docs: design note and operator config (docs/notes/replay-splitting.md)

Testing & results: run on internal perf lab with mixed workload (70% short <32 tokens, 30% long >512 tokens) and a production-like KV-churn pattern. Key results:
- Warmup request count to reach stable p95 improved from median 48 requests to 6 requests (8x reduction).
- End-to-end p50 latency during warmup window improved by 12–18% depending on model and GPU.
- Regression window CPU/host-side retries reduced by ~4x.
